proposals.hypothesis: Adding F to the D07 Cl2 scaffold raised f from 1.24 to 1.32-1.38, while heavier halogens (Br, D11 f=0.28; Cl4, D14 f=0.72) lowered it. Swapping both Cl for F should keep the strong CO2 binding of the 2,6-disubstituted BQ (D07 bind -25.8 kcal/mol) with a smaller steric footprint. The F4 core D08 has margin 0.178, so margin should rise above D07's 0.097. Aiming for f>=2 is a stretch, and this tests whether less halogen mass helps f.

D08 (F4) has f=1.03, margin 0.178 and no detachment. D07, with two ring H atoms, has the higher f of 1.24. Removing one F leaves a trifluoro-BQ with one H, to test whether an open ring site raises f toward D07's level while F keeps the margin above 0.15. Heavier halogenation lowered f (D14, D11), so I expect f to rise as halogen count falls.

proposals.hypothesis: A mixed F2Cl2 pattern with Cl and F alternating around the ring. The nearby F2Cl2 isomers had f=1.32 (margin 0.26) and f=1.17 (margin 0.22), both with no detachment. This is a new substitution pattern, in which Cl at the para-related positions retains the Cl-driven binding of D07 and F keeps f up. Mixed F/Cl has never lowered f below 1.1 in the history. It probes whether the pattern gives a margin above 0.15 with f>1.3.

Monofluorination of D07 (f 1.24 to 1.38) and difluorination (f 1.32) both raised f and margin. Here one Cl is removed and two F are added, giving a mono-Cl difluoro-BQ with one open H. This reduces heavy-halogen load, which lowered f in D14 and D11, while the F pair raises the margin toward 0.18-0.26. It tests whether Cl count is the lever for f at fixed F.

D15 (phenanthrenequinone) has f=1.09 and bind -27.9 kcal/mol, the strongest CO2 binding, but its margin is -0.196. Dichlorination (2,7) raised the margin to -0.017 but lowered f to 0.82. Chlorinating only one outer ring should cost less f, since the first Cl gives most of the benefit per halogen. Margin should rise by about half of the dichloro gain, which probably still falls short of 0.15. It tests the f/margin trade-off on the ortho-quinone core, and the margin is the risk here.
